documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32M here for yearly exam. No complaints. Colitis has been quiet, no flares this year by his account. GI visit coming up next month. Still on mesalamine 1.2 g twice daily, rarely misses a dose. Work is steady.

NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: Well appearing. Eyes anicteric. No neck masses. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Extremities without edema. Skin clear.

PHQ-2 0.

Assessment/plan:
- UC on mesalamine, followed by GI. Annual BMP for kidney function today with CBC and lipids.
- Flu and COVID in October, nurse visit.
- Back next fall.

documents.title: Results

documents.body: Hi Austin, everything from Tuesday came back normal: counts, kidneys, electrolytes, cholesterol. Have a good GI visit next month.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP
Date of service: 10/14/2024
Re: Austin Crowley, DOB 04/05/1992

Dear Doctor,

I saw Austin today for his yearly ulcerative colitis visit. He was diagnosed in 2015 and has taken mesalamine the whole time. He is taking it as prescribed and has gone the past year without a flare. He has had no blood in his stool recently, no abdominal pain and no weight loss.

Medications: mesalamine DR 1.2 g by mouth twice daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal grandmother with ulcerative colitis; father with primary sclerosing cholangitis; mother with autoimmune hypothyroidism.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, financial analyst.

Vital signs were stable. On exam the abdomen is nontender without masses.

CBC and basic metabolic panel drawn today are normal.

Impression: ulcerative colitis in clinical remission on mesalamine.
Plan: continue mesalamine 1.2 g twice daily. Return in one year, sooner for any change in bowel habits or bleeding.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: GI visit and MRI
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted to give you a heads up. I saw GI on the 6th because I've been tired and itchy for months. My liver tests came back off and they had me do an MRI of the bile ducts on Friday. GI called and said it looks like PSC, which is what my dad has. They're sending you a letter. I still need to rebook my physical too. Can we talk about all of it when the letter comes?

documents.title: RE: GI visit and MRI
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, Austin. That is a lot to take in, especially with your dad's history. Once GI's note and the MRI report arrive I'll read them and we can sit down; I'll have the front desk find you a slot in the next couple of weeks and we'll do the physical separately. Your flu shot is still on for Wednesday, that's fine to get. Text me if anything changes before then.

conditions.label: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
conditions.note: Diagnosed by outside GI on MRCP.

reports.text:
OUTSIDE IMAGING REPORT
Exam: MRI abdomen without and with contrast, MRCP protocol.
Indication: Cholestatic liver tests in a patient with ulcerative colitis.
Technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MR imaging of the abdomen with 2D and 3D MRCP sequences before and after IV gadolinium.
Findings: Multiple short strictures involve the intrahepatic ducts of both lobes and the extrahepatic bile duct, with intervening segments of dilation. No discrete intraductal filling defect. Liver normal in size and signal without focal lesion. Gallbladder unremarkable. Pancreas normal; pancreatic duct not dilated. Spleen normal in size. No ascites. No lymphadenopathy. Kidneys and adrenals unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Multifocal intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary strictures with segmental dilations, in keeping with primary sclerosing cholangitis.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GASTROENTEROLOGY GROUP
Dates: clinic visit 10/06/2025; MRCP 10/17/2025
Re: Austin Crowley, DOB 04/05/1992

Dear Doctor,

Austin came back to clinic with roughly six months of fatigue and itching. On questioning he also described on-and-off bloody diarrhea going back to late last year, which he had put down to hemorrhoids and had not mentioned to anyone. He continues mesalamine DR 1.2 g twice daily. He denies travel, alcohol or sexual risk exposures.

Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: maternal grandmother with UC, father with PSC, mother with autoimmune hypothyroidism.

Exam: well nourished, jaundiced. Abdomen soft, not distended, nontender. No hepatosplenomegaly. No ascites.

Labs 10/06/2025:
Total bilirubin 2.1 mg/dL (H)
Direct bilirubin 1.5 mg/dL (H)
Alkaline phosphatase 420 U/L (H)
GGT 210 U/L (H)
AST 50 U/L (H)
ALT 55 U/L

MRCP 10/17/2025: multifocal strictures of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts with segmental dilation (report enclosed).

Impression: primary sclerosing cholangitis in a patient with long-standing ulcerative colitis and a father with PSC. Cholestatic liver enzymes with mild hyperbilirubinemia.

Plan: continue mesalamine 1.2 g twice daily. We discussed the diagnosis with him by phone after the MRCP. Follow-up in clinic in six months with repeat labs, sooner if jaundice or itching worsens.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.

Gastroenterology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here to go over the new PSC diagnosis. GI letter and MRCP report reviewed with him. He has been tired and itchy since around the spring and figured it was work stress. The bloody stool episodes GI wrote about he had brushed off as hemorrhoids; GI is aware. He knows PSC well from his father and has a lot of questions about what comes next. Still on mesalamine 1.2 g BID. No other meds. NKDA. No alcohol.

O: Vitals as charted, weight unchanged. Sclerae faintly yellow. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly, no ascites. No edema.

A/P:
1. Primary sclerosing cholangitis, new, GI managing. Labs and MRCP reviewed, bilirubin 2.1 and alk phos 420. Talked through how it is usually followed with labs and imaging and that GI will lead. Added to problem list. Asked him to message me or GI right away for fever, worse yellowing, or right-sided belly pain.
2. UC on mesalamine, per GI.
3. Vaccines for chronic liver disease: hep B series already complete (2023). Hep A dose 1 today, dose 2 in 6 months. PCV20 today.
4. Physical still to be rebooked, front desk to schedule December.

~35 minutes, more than half counseling.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
33M, physical, rebooked from August.

Interval: PSC diagnosed in October by GI, seen here 11/4. Fatigue and itching ongoing, about the same. GI follow-up planned for spring with labs. Mesalamine 1.2 g BID continues.

Mood ok, a little down about the diagnosis but coping, talking with family. Sleeping fine. PHQ-2 1.

NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: Well appearing, no distress. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. No edema. Skin with no rash.

Plan:
- PSC and UC per GI. Liver labs with GI in the spring, not repeating here.
- BMP for mesalamine, CBC.
- Vaccines: flu, COVID done this fall. PCV20 and hep A #1 given 11/4; hep A #2 due May.
- RTC 1 year, or sooner.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Blood counts and kidney function from your physical are normal. Liver tests stay with GI as we discussed.
